messages:
claire: Heads up — noticed weird midtail behavior in the console for a few endpoints.
claire: p95 jumps when we include KV cache hits for short prefix requests, but p99 barely moves. Feels like we're mixing request classes.
sam: can you paste an example slice? curious about request lengths + prefix patterns.
claire: yep — e.g. client A src=web route=/chat.prefix/foo short prompts get 30ms (kvcache hit), others 120ms. Console p95 for the whole endpoint drops ~25ms when hits included.
ben: that suggests the distribution is multi-modal. If we lump everything the p95 shifts but p99 still dominated by long tail.
violet: Are these KV cache hits being tagged in telemetry? we should be able to break out by sample origin.
claire: we have sample_origin tags (kvcache, cold, cached_prefix) but the console rollup currently only exposes origin at a coarse level.
sam: Proposal: surface a "decompose by request prefix" option in the latency pane that splits percentile lines by prefix buckets (first 8 chars or route param). Also add a toggle "include KV cache hits".
ben: UX wise, showing separate lines for prefix buckets could be noisy. Maybe default to top-3 prefixes + "other".
violet: agreed. backend needs to support the query: group by prefix and compute p50/p95/p99 with proper sampling weights. current rollups use t-digest merged across samples which assume same population distribution.
claire: the tricky part: our sampling is heavier on cold requests; kvcache hits are less sampled. If we just merge t-digests we bias percentiles.
sam: right — we either need to surface sample counts and effective weights or materialize separate t-digests per (route, prefix, origin) at ingestion.
ben: quick backend sketch:
```
GROUP BY route, prefix, origin
STORE t_digest -> periodic rollup window (1m)
EXPOSE query param: ?decompose=prefix&topk=3&include_kvcache=true
```
ben: When include_kvcache=false, query excludes origin=kvcache from the merge entirely.
violet: also need to ensure alerting/SLOs still use canonical merge (include_kvcache=false by default for SLOs?) or have a flag per SLO.
claire: For console labels: show sample_count and an icon that explains sampling bias. e.g. "samples: 412 (est. coverage: 8%)" and a tooltip.
sam: We should add a lightweight experiment: enable decompose UI for one org and log user clicks + confusion; backend will respond with precomputed prefix rollups.
ben: Implementation tasks:
- infra: rollup per (route,prefix,origin) (ben)
- api: add query params + sampling-aware merge (sam)
- ui: decompose toggle, top-k dropdown, sample_count badge + tooltip (violet)
- docs: note sampling caveats + SLO guidance (claire)

claire: can we estimate storage increase? storing t-digest per prefix upsamples cardinality.
ben: rough math: routes ~2000, avg prefixes per route we care about ~5, origins ~3 -> 2000*5*3 ~30k rollups/minute. t-digests are small, should be fine but validate.
violet: UI mock: small stacked bar showing p50/p95/p99 for each prefix with hover showing counts + origin breakdown. Also a checkbox: "Normalize by sample weight" that switches to weighted merge.
sam: we need to be careful — weighted merge needs provenance: each t-digest must carry sample_count and total_count estimates.
claire: ok owner assignments agreed above. Ben/Sam, can you sync on an API spec? propose: POST /internal/latency/rollup_spec and GET /internal/latency?decompose=prefix...
ben: will draft tonight.
claire: violet — can you mock two variants (line chart vs stacked bars) by EOD Fri?
violet: yep.
sam: one more note: telemetry should start tagging request_prefix at ingress (first N bytes) so we can standardize. add a privacy check — don't include PII.
claire: good call, use hashed prefix or normalized token.
claire: Thanks all — this should clarify p95 anomalies that keep confusing product.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rollup-ingester v2 -> staging at 2867004600 :rocket:
ben: merging api PR to staging now.
sam: I'll follow up with spec link in this thread.
claire: great, mark as actioned once spec + mock links posted. thanks!
